Trust expiry uses clock_timestamp() in a fresh statement after lock acquisition, not transaction-start NOW(). Lock order is user, sessions, trust, matching successful OTP completion. Trust failure precedes session-cap eviction and inserts, so rejected trust cannot revoke an old session or create a new one.

Real PostgreSQL concurrency tests hold the account while password, revocation, expiry, address or staff status changes. Concurrent duplicate deletion produces one success, one not-found response and one audit entry. Removing trust requires OTP on the next password login and leaves already-issued sessions active; the UI explains that distinction.

steps.summary: Audit device-trust grants atomically, reject OTP expiry across lock waits, and verify T-02.01.03 locally.
review: Compared T-02.01.03 with the controller, OTP/account locking, session creation, optional trust, resend limits and the shared inline OTP UI. Challenges are purpose/account/version-bound; wrong guesses durably decrement the locked challenge. A consumed or exhausted code cannot authorize a new session. Staff always require OTP; customer trust remains risk-based under the locally verified T-02.01.02 policy.

Device opt-in now writes device_trust_granted in the same transaction as OTP consumption, session/refresh insertion and the trust upsert. RETURNING id identifies the actual persisted row when an existing device is renewed. Audit metadata contains only its record ID, with actor, correlation and observed IP; no raw browser proof or fingerprint hash. Opt-out does not alter or audit trust.

Challenge validity is checked again after waiting for the account lock. A final database wall-clock check after session/trust/audit writes rejects expiry during later waits and rolls back every effect. User, session and trust locks retain their existing order; the challenge lock prevents concurrent replay throughout the transaction.

Real PostgreSQL tests cover audit failure for both new and existing trust, preserved challenge attempts, no partial sessions/refreshes/cookies, unchanged prior trust and successful concurrent retry with exactly one grant audit. Separate account/session/trust waits cross the challenge deadline and leave the old session/trust unchanged with no grant audit.

A new HTTP test sends five concurrent incorrect codes, confirms zero attempts, observes the independent IP transport limit, then clears only the isolated transport counters and proves the exhausted challenge still rejects the correct OTP.
